summary: A Yes vote authorizes the district to issue bonds for School Facilities Improvement District No. 1, repaid by property taxes within that district.

tax.text: A yes vote authorizes $33.8 million in bonds and an estimated property-tax levy of $29 per $100,000 of assessed value for school facilities.
tax.quote: shall Merced Union High School District's School Facilities Improvement District No. 1 measure authorizing $33,800,000 in bonds, at legal rates, and levying approximately $29 per $100,000 assessed value ($2,025,000 annually), while outstanding, be adopted

schools.text: A yes vote funds classroom, school-facility, safety, career-technical education, roofing, and plumbing improvements within the district.
schools.quote: To improve the quality of education; construct, upgrade, and modernize classrooms, restrooms, and school facilities; make safety/security improvements; renovate or construct career technical education classrooms

tax.text: The No position opposes authorizing $33.8 million in school bonds that would be secured by a property-tax increase.
tax.quote: A “NO” vote means the voter is against authorizing the Merced Union High School District to issue and sell up to $33,800,000 in general obligation bonds.
